title: WHY OBADIAH HID ONE HUNDRED PROPHETS IN CAVES
paragraphs: WHY OBADIAH HID ONE HUNDRED PROPHETS IN CAVES

The story of Obadiah is hidden between political corruption, spiritual compromise, murder plots, and one of the darkest periods in Israel's history. It is a story that many believers read quickly and forget. Yet buried inside this account is one of the most courageous acts of faith recorded in Scripture.
But to keep God's voice alive when an entire nation was trying to silence it.
And the reason he hid one hundred prophets in caves reveals something powerful about how God works in seasons when evil seems to be winning.
The story unfolds during the reign of King Ahab and Queen Jezebel.
Scripture introduces Obadiah with remarkable words:

“Now Obadiah feared the LORD greatly.”
(1 Kings 18:3)
This was not occasional church attendance.
The Hebrew word יָרֵא (yare) carries the idea of profound awe, loyalty, devotion, and covenant faithfulness.
Obadiah lived in a palace that opposed God.
Yet his heart belonged entirely to God.
Every day he worked under King Ahab.
Every day he served inside a government increasingly hostile to the worship of Yahweh.
Every day he watched darkness advance.

“For when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the LORD...”
(1 Kings 18:4)
The phrase “cut off” comes from the Hebrew word כָּרַת (karath), often meaning to destroy, eliminate, or exterminate.
This was not merely political opposition.
She was not satisfied with disagreement.
History has repeatedly demonstrated that whenever darkness gains power, one of its first targets is truth.
Yet God always preserves a remnant.
While Jezebel hunted prophets, God had already positioned Obadiah.

“Obadiah took one hundred prophets and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.”
(1 Kings 18:4)
This was not a one-time act.
Every day could be his last.
Because he understood something many believers forget.
Sometimes faithfulness looks less like standing on a stage and more like protecting what God treasures.
While others protected their positions, he protected God's servants.
While others saved themselves, he risked himself.
That kind of faith rarely receives applause.
One of the fascinating aspects of this account is that Obadiah never performed a public miracle.
Elijah called down fire from heaven.
Yet both were essential to God's plan.
Many Christians underestimate the importance of hidden obedience.
They believe significance only exists where visibility exists.
The kingdom of God is built not merely by famous voices but by faithful hearts.
Some believers are called to stand on Mount Carmel.
Others are called to sustain those who do.
When Elijah eventually meets Obadiah, another remarkable detail emerges.
He fears being associated with Elijah because Ahab is desperately searching for him.
This fear does not mean Obadiah lacked faith.
It means courage was operating in the presence of fear.
Biblical courage is not the absence of fear.
Many people imagine heroes as fearless individuals.
And perhaps that is where many readers find themselves today.
You may not be facing a queen determined to execute prophets.
But perhaps you know what it feels like to remain faithful in hostile environments.
A workplace that mocks biblical convictions.
A culture increasingly uncomfortable with truth.
A season where standing for Christ carries consequences.
Obadiah reminds us that God sees hidden faithfulness.
Every quiet act of obedience matters.
Nothing done for Christ is wasted.
The New Testament reveals this principle even more fully through Jesus.
The Greek word often translated as faithful is πιστός (pistos).
It describes someone trustworthy, loyal, dependable, steadfast.
Jesus consistently celebrates this kind of faithfulness.
That truth becomes even more beautiful when viewed through the Gospel.
Because every story of hidden rescue ultimately points toward Jesus Christ.
Obadiah risked his life to save one hundred prophets.
Jesus gave His life to save sinners.
Obadiah brought bread and water into caves.
Jesus became the Bread of Life.
Obadiah protected God's servants from earthly death.
The greatest rescue story was never in a cave.
There, the scandal of human sin collided with the grace of God.
There, guilty people found forgiveness through the blood of Christ.
The Gospel is God's ultimate declaration that no darkness is powerful enough to stop His plan.
That is why the story of Obadiah still matters.
It reminds us that God often works through ordinary people who choose extraordinary faithfulness.
The world may never know their names.
History books may never celebrate them.
But heaven records every act of obedience.
And perhaps today, more than ever, God is looking for modern-day Obadiahs.
People willing to stand firm when compromise is easier.
People willing to protect truth when culture opposes it.
People willing to serve Christ even when nobody notices.
People who fear God more than public opinion.
If this message challenged you, don't let it stop here.
Your testimony may encourage someone else who feels alone.
The mission is simple: proclaim biblical truth, make disciples, strengthen believers, and point people to Jesus Christ.
Because one act of faithfulness may preserve far more than you can see.
Because one quiet act of obedience may echo into eternity.
Because somewhere, even now, God is still looking for people like Obadiah.
The God who saw Obadiah sees you.
